Analysis.object: In the final model, all variables together explained 17% of the variation in EAT-26 scores. These results suggest that concern with body weight and physical appearance and a high level of psychological commitment to exercise are predictors of unhealthy eating habits in athletes.
One limitation of this study was the small sample size, a fact impairing generalization of the results.
Future studies that include larger samples and additional aesthetic modalities and that evaluate the influence of others factors on the eating behavior of athletes are needed.

Population.object: Criteria for inclusion in the study were a consent form signed by the responsible person; a training frequency of at least 5 days per week in the respective modality; with a minimum duration of 2h/training; participation in at least one regional competition in 2011, and voluntary agreement to answer the questionnaires and to participate in the anthropometric assessments
